title: Building Sovereign AI Agents on Private Infrastructure
summary: Sovereign AI agents allow you to maintain absolute ownership of your data and model weights by running autonomous systems on local hardware.
body_markdown:
## Deploying sovereign AI workflows with Activepieces


Activepieces includes SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, and audit logs in its air-gapped build exactly as they appear in the managed cloud, ensuring that organizations requiring the most control do not receive a fraction of the product.


By keeping the logic and execution engine within your own infrastructure, you maintain physical control over the triggers and actions that drive your AI agents. Organizations like MoneyGram and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production to maintain this level of environmental sovereignty.


### Deploying workflows within your private infrastructure


Activepieces provides an MIT-licensed core that can be deployed via Docker Compose or Kubernetes, ensuring that every workflow execution remains behind the corporate firewall.


This open foundation allows you to deploy an unlimited number of automated runs on your own hardware without per-execution fees.


When security mandates are at their strictest, the platform supports air-gapped installations where the network cable is pulled.


A comparison of the enterprise feature list (including SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, and secret managers) in the self-hosted air-gapped documentation against the managed cloud shows the same governance capabilities are available in both environments.


### Connecting local LLMs to private business apps


Every credential Activepieces touches (API keys, OAuth tokens, and connection secrets) can be routed to your own external secret manager in the self-hosted edition, ensuring that no vendor holds the credentials your business runs on.


Because the orchestrator lives on the same local network as the model weights, sensitive data never leaves the premises during the inference process.


Configure a self-hosted instance against an external secret manager and inspect the Activepieces database yourself; you will find that the credentials are not there, as the platform supports externalizing these secrets alongside its custom RBAC and audit log governance.


In the screenshot of a successful run, you can see this localized control where an "Instance Stopped" trigger immediately fires a "Revoke Token" action.


The Run Details panel confirms the specific duration and the exact JSON payload sent to the Squareup API. It provides a granular view of how the AI interacts with external services.


Verifying that the agent is performing only authorized actions is made possible by this visibility.


### Enterprise governance: SSO, RBAC, and Audit Logs for AI


The Community edition provides the foundation for self-hosted automation. Regulated organizations require centralized control over who can build or execute AI workflows. Activepieces is equipped with enterprise-grade governance features to manage these risks at scale.


Through Single Sign-On (SSO) and SCIM, access to AI orchestration is tied to your corporate identity provider. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) restricts the ability to modify critical flows or access sensitive API secrets to specific verified personnel.


Audit Logs record every change to a workflow and every execution attempt. They provide the necessary paper trail for your compliance officers.


If you require these governance layers or specialized support for air-gapped deployments, you can coordinate with the[Activepieces sales team](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) to align the software with your internal security architecture.
